reasons: The cited clause squarely triggers rule LD: Section 7.7 requires Customer to pay Vendor 15% of annual Fees per week 'as liquidated damages,' triggered by a ten-day payment delay — a Customer-payable LD that fails both the preferred (none) and fallback (single early-termination amount capped at 3 months' fees) positions and compounds into walk-away territory.
Direction is correct: the LD runs against us (Customer), not in our favour, so this is not an over-flag of a Vendor-side service credit or an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the playbook position by deleting the liquidated damages and substituting customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, which is the standard commercial replacement rather than a bare deletion that would leave no late-payment remedy; the high changed-character ratio (0.859) is explained by the rule requiring replacement of the operative sentence.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and explains both the change and the rationale (punitive, could exceed contract value); the cross-reference to the Section 7.3 withholding right is consistent with the added 'proper, undisputed invoice' qualifier.

Minor scope creep worth noting but not disqualifying: the edit also extends the grace period from ten to thirty days and fixes an interest rate of 1% per month, and it invokes 'Applicable Law' which is not shown as a resolved definition — confirm that term exists in the agreement and be prepared to concede the 30-day grace if the counterparty pushes back.
